competition_overview.research_objective: Connect 10 Hz NFL Scouting Combine wearable sensor tracking data (`combine_tracking.csv`) and standardized Combine drill scores (`combine_results.csv`) with regular-season NFL game performance (`player_play.csv`, `game_tracking_2023/2024/2025.csv`, `player_career_successes.csv`) across five core position groups: Wide Receivers (WR), Tight Ends (TE), Defensive Backs (DB), Offensive Linemen (OL), and Defensive Linemen (DL).
competition_overview.problem_paradigm: Analytical & Research-Oriented Discovery Challenge — Unlike conventional single-column supervised leaderboard competitions, the NFL Big Data Bowl evaluates teams on the originality, statistical rigor, football actionability, and visualization clarity of their research framework connecting pre-draft Combine movement traits to regular-season NFL performance.
competition_overview.target_column_policy: Do not assume a single mandatory target column exists. While `player_career_successes.csv` and `player_play.csv` provide official career and play-level outcome benchmarks, researchers may formulate specific kinematic transfer metrics, route/trench efficiency outcomes, or career milestone models appropriate to their chosen position group and drill hypothesis.

position_groups.name: Wide Receivers
position_groups.focus: Linear release burst, top-end speed maintenance, braking impulse entering route breaks, and exit velocity retention.

position_groups.name: Tight Ends
position_groups.focus: Size-adjusted acceleration, hybrid inline blocking momentum vs. route-break separation efficiency.

position_groups.name: Defensive Backs
position_groups.focus: Backpedal-to-sprint hip-turn angular velocity (`do/dt`), lateral strafe fluidity (`|o - dir|`), and closing burst.

position_groups.name: Offensive Linemen
position_groups.focus: First-step 0.5s pass-set impulse, lateral mirror-and-slide agility, and mass-adjusted momentum.

position_groups.name: Defensive Linemen
position_groups.focus: First-step pass-rush get-off (`0.0s-0.5s` burst), 3-cone bend/cornering curvature, and power-to-mass ratio.

research_questions.title: Combine Deceleration & Braking Efficiency vs. NFL Route Separation (WR / TE)
research_questions.question: Does a prospect's braking efficiency and transition time during the Combine 3-cone and 20-yard short shuttle drills provide incremental information about regular-season route-break velocity retention beyond traditional stopwatch drill times?
research_questions.why_it_matters: Stopwatch times conflate linear straight-line speed with change-of-direction mechanics. Two wide receivers with identical 7.00s 3-cone times may exhibit drastically different deceleration profiles entering the cone vs. re-acceleration exiting the break. On NFL passing downs, separation on sharp-breaking routes (Out, Dig, Comeback, Hitch) depends on minimizing deceleration warnings (sink-and-brake phase) and retaining exit velocity.
exact_columns: combine_tracking.csv: nflId, drillType, frameId, x, y, s, a, o, dir, event
game_tracking_2023/2024/2025.csv: gameId, playId, nflId, frameId, s, a, o, dir, event
required_joins: players.csv (nflId) -> combine_tracking.csv (nflId) [1:N frame-level; aggregate to player-drill before joining to play outcomes]
player_play.csv (gameId, playId, nflId) -> game_tracking_YYYY.csv (gameId, playId, nflId) [1:N frame-level]
proposed_features: FE-02: Braking Deceleration Impulse & Entry-to-Exit Speed Ratio
FE-03: Orientation-Direction Divergence (|o - dir| CoD Fluidity)
FE-07: In-Game Route-Break Velocity Retention Index
suggested_visualizations: Phase-aligned velocity (s) and tangential acceleration (ds/dt) curves around Combine cone turns vs. stopwatch quartiles.
Bivariate partial-dependence contour of Combine Braking Efficiency vs. NFL Route-Break Velocity Retention stratified by WR/TE.
statistical_and_ml_methods: Functional Data Analysis (FDA) / B-spline registration of 10 Hz velocity curves around apex turns.

Hierarchical Bayesian mixed-effects regression predicting play-level route break exit speed with random intercepts for player (`nflId`) and route type (`routeRan`), testing incremental likelihood ratio over stopwatch `threeConeDrill`.
confounders_and_leakage_risks: Selection bias: Elite WR prospects increasingly opt out of agility drills at the Combine.
Tactical confounding: Press vs. off-man coverage and defensive double-teams alter in-game route deceleration.
Temporal leakage hazard: Must strictly ensure Combine tracking precedes the regular-season seasons evaluated.
research_questions.sample_size_considerations: Requires filtering to WR/TE prospects who both completed Combine agility tracking and logged sufficient regular-season route snaps (>= 100 routes ran).
research_questions.validation_strategy: Draft-cohort out-of-sample cross-validation (e.g., train on earlier draft classes, evaluate rank-order calibration on subsequent rookie cohorts) and bootstrap confidence intervals over player clusters.

supporting_or_weakening_evidence.supports: Out-of-sample partial R^2 or C-index improvement (>0.03) when adding 10 Hz braking features to a baseline model containing stopwatch 3-cone and 40-yard dash times.
supporting_or_weakening_evidence.weakens: High collinearity (r > 0.90) between sensor braking integrals and simple stopwatch times, or low test-retest stability across game seasons.

research_questions.known_limitations: Cannot claim causal interventions without accounting for collegiate coaching and NFL offensive scheme role assignment.
research_questions.feasibility_status: Feasible (Requires local download and profiling of combine_tracking.csv, player_play.csv, and game_tracking CSVs)

research_questions.title: First-Step Kinematic Impulse in Trench Prospects (OL / DL) & Pass-Rush / Pass-Set Translation
research_questions.question: How well do initial 0.0s–0.5s acceleration impulse and body-mass-adjusted momentum during Combine drills predict post-snap first-step burst and trench engagement kinematics for Offensive and Defensive Linemen in NFL regular-season games?
research_questions.why_it_matters: For OL and DL prospects, the final 40-yard dash time (30–40 yards downfield) is biomechanically unrepresentative of trench play, which occurs within 1.5 seconds and 3–5 yards of the line of scrimmage. Even the 10-yard split is a coarse cumulative timer. 10 Hz sensor tracking allows measuring peak initial acceleration (`a` in frames 1–5), jerk (`da/dt`), and mass-adjusted momentum (`weight * s`).
exact_columns: combine_tracking.csv: nflId, drillType, frameId, s, a, dis, o, dir
game_tracking_2023/2024/2025.csv: gameId, playId, nflId, frameId, s, a, o, dir, event
proposed_features: FE-01: First-Step Peak Acceleration & Jerk (0.0s-0.5s Window)
FE-05: Mass-Adjusted Peak Kinetic Energy & Momentum Proxy
FE-06: Position-Group Z-Score & Mahalanobis Kinematic Distance
suggested_visualizations: Mass vs. Initial 0.5s Peak Acceleration Pareto frontier for DL and OL prospects.
Comparison of Combine 0.5s burst percentile vs. NFL regular-season post-`ball_snap` 0.5s burst percentile.
statistical_and_ml_methods: Quantile regression (90th percentile in-game burst as a function of Combine 0.5s impulse) to account for play-effort variance.
Regularized ElasticNet / Gradient Boosted Survival or Ordinal models linking trench impulse to `player_career_successes.csv` benchmarks.
confounders_and_leakage_risks: Stance confounding: 3-point stance in the 40-yard dash vs. 2-point pass-set stance for offensive tackles.

Play-call effort: Linemen do not sprint at 100% capacity on screen plays or run blocks away from play side; using mean in-game speed instead of 90th/95th percentile post-snap burst introduces severe attenuation bias.
research_questions.sample_size_considerations: Separate interior DL (DT/NT) from edge rushers (DE) and interior OL (OG/C) from offensive tackles (OT) where sample sizes permit.
research_questions.validation_strategy: Leave-one-draft-class-out validation; stability correlation (ICC) between 2023, 2024, and 2025 regular-season post-snap burst.

supporting_or_weakening_evidence.supports: Stronger rank correlation (Spearman rho) between Combine 0.0-0.5s sensor impulse and NFL 95th-percentile post-snap burst than with stopwatch 10-yard split.
supporting_or_weakening_evidence.weakens: High noise or frame-alignment jitter in the first 3 frames of `combine_tracking.csv` relative to `ball_snap` in game tracking.

research_questions.known_limitations: RFID tags mounted in shoulder pads measure torso translation, not independent foot strike or hand punch timing.

research_questions.title: Defensive Back Hip-Flip Fluidity & Backpedal-to-Sprint Transition Mechanics (DB)
research_questions.question: Can angular velocity of body orientation (`do/dt`) and minimal speed loss during Combine backpedal-and-turn drills quantify 'hip fluidity' in Defensive Backs and predict in-game phase maintenance against vertical and breaking routes?
research_questions.why_it_matters: Scouts routinely describe cornerbacks and safeties as having 'fluid' or 'stiff' hips, a qualitative judgment rarely captured by linear stopwatch tests. During Combine positional drills and agility tests, 10 Hz orientation (`o`) and motion direction (`dir`) vectors directly measure how rapidly a DB can rotate their torso by 180 degrees while minimizing translational deceleration.
exact_columns: combine_tracking.csv: nflId, drillType, frameId, s, a, o, dir
game_tracking_2023/2024/2025.csv: gameId, playId, nflId, frameId, x, y, s, a, o, dir
required_joins: player_play.csv (gameId, playId, nflId) -> game_tracking_YYYY.csv (gameId, playId, nflId)
proposed_features: FE-03: Orientation-Direction Divergence (|o - dir| CoD Fluidity)
FE-04: Peak Angular Hip-Turn Velocity & Transition Speed Retention
suggested_visualizations: Polar phase plot of torso orientation (`o`) vs. movement direction (`dir`) during Combine DB drills.
Speed retention curve across the [-0.5s, +0.5s] window centered on peak angular rotation (`max |do/dt|`).
statistical_and_ml_methods: Circular statistics (von Mises kernel smoothing) on unwrapped orientation angles.
Mixed-effects modeling of in-game coverage transition speed loss on passing plays.
confounders_and_leakage_risks: Coverage scheme confounding: Zone coverage (eyes on quarterback, backpedal posture) exhibits fundamentally different `|o - dir|` signatures than press-man trail technique.
Angle wrap-around artifact: Naive subtraction of `o` across the 0/360 degree boundary produces artificial 359-degree spikes if not unwrapped via `atan2(sin(Δθ), cos(Δθ))`.
research_questions.sample_size_considerations: Ensure DB drills in `combine_tracking.csv` have sufficient frame density around transition events.
research_questions.validation_strategy: Split-half reliability across multiple Combine drill attempts and cross-season consistency in NFL coverage snaps.

supporting_or_weakening_evidence.supports: High intra-player reliability (ICC > 0.65) of transition speed retention during high `|do/dt|` events between Combine and NFL games.
supporting_or_weakening_evidence.weakens: Sensor orientation `o` jitter during rapid shoulder-pad rotation exceeding the 10 Hz Nyquist frequency for sub-0.2s turns.

research_questions.known_limitations: 10 Hz sampling (100 ms per frame) sets a physical resolution limit on sub-100ms micro-movements.

research_questions.title: Combine Underwear Speed vs. Functional Padded Game Speed (All 5 Position Groups)
research_questions.question: How stable is the rank ordering of peak velocity and acceleration between unpadded Combine drills and padded regular-season NFL games across WR, TE, DB, OL, and DL cohorts, and which kinematic traits exhibit the smallest context-transfer decay?
research_questions.why_it_matters: A central debate in NFL scouting is 'track speed vs. play speed'—prospects who run fast in shorts on a predetermined track at the Combine may slow down disproportionately when wearing pads, reading keys, and reacting to contact on an NFL field.
proposed_features: FE-08: Combine-to-Game Kinematic Transfer Ratio (Functional Play Speed Retention)
suggested_visualizations: Bland-Altman agreement plots and dumbbell rank-shift charts comparing Combine 99th-percentile speed vs. NFL 99th-percentile speed by position group.
statistical_and_ml_methods: Intraclass Correlation Coefficients (ICC) and Spearman rank stability across position groups.
Errors-in-variables regression accounting for opportunity volume (number of NFL snaps played) via empirical Bayes shrinkage.
confounders_and_leakage_risks: Opportunity/snap-count bias: Sample maximum (`max(s)`) is an order statistic that grows monotonically with sample size (total frames played). A backup WR with 30 snaps will have a downward-biased empirical `max(s)` compared to a starter with 800 snaps.
Survivorship bias: Only prospects who make an NFL roster and earn regular-season snaps appear in `game_tracking_2023/2024/2025.csv`.
research_questions.sample_size_considerations: Use exposure-adjusted quantiles or extreme-value theory (Generalized Pareto Distribution) rather than raw sample maxima to compare players with unequal snap counts.
research_questions.validation_strategy: Subsample equal numbers of plays per player (e.g., 50 random plays) via Monte Carlo resampling to eliminate snap-volume bias.

supporting_or_weakening_evidence.supports: Consistent rank preservation (rho > 0.70) after controlling for snap exposure, or identification of specific Combine sub-phases that predict positive transfer.
supporting_or_weakening_evidence.weakens: Severe range restriction among drafted NFL starters obscuring bivariate correlations without Heckman or inverse-probability-of-censoring adjustments.

research_questions.known_limitations: Unobserved injury history between Combine and regular season can depress functional game speed.

research_questions.title: Multivariate Kinematic Archetypes vs. Career Outcomes & Survivorship Bias Adjustment
research_questions.question: After adjusting for draft-selection and roster survivorship bias, which multi-dimensional Combine sensor archetypes (combining burst, braking efficiency, angular fluidity, and size) are associated with superior longitudinal outcomes in `player_career_successes.csv`?
research_questions.why_it_matters: Evaluating Combine metrics solely on NFL starters suffers from classic Berkson's / collider stratification bias (often cited in sports analytics as the 'draft selection paradox'). Because NFL front offices already select players using traditional stopwatch metrics (`combine_results.csv`), conditioning on NFL snap volume can artificially attenuate the apparent effect of known metrics while highlighting orthogonal sensor traits that scouts previously under-weighted.
exact_columns: players.csv: nflId, position, height, weight, birthDate
combine_tracking.csv: nflId, drillType, s, a, o, dir
player_career_successes.csv: nflId and career outcome columns
proposed_features: FE-05: Mass-Adjusted Peak Kinetic Energy & Momentum Proxy
FE-06: Position-Group Z-Score & Mahalanobis Kinematic Distance
suggested_visualizations: Parallel coordinates / radar profile of Combine sensor archetypes by position group.
Comparison of unadjusted vs. Inverse Probability of Censoring Weighted (IPCW) effect estimates on career success outcomes.
statistical_and_ml_methods: Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM) or regularized PCA within each position group to extract orthogonal movement components (Linear Burst, Braking Control, Angular Fluidity, Mass-Momentum).
Two-stage Heckman selection model or Inverse Probability Weighting (IPW) modeling the probability of logging regular-season snaps before modeling career success metrics.
confounders_and_leakage_risks: Draft capital confounding: High draft picks receive guaranteed roster spots and more early-career snaps regardless of rookie efficiency.
Right-censoring: 2024 and 2025 draft cohorts have fewer elapsed NFL seasons than 2023 cohorts; outcome metrics in `player_career_successes.csv` must be normalized by cohort exposure.
research_questions.sample_size_considerations: Bounded by total number of prospects in `combine_results.csv` (~41 KB) and `player_career_successes.csv` (~13.8 KB), likely several hundred prospects total across the 5 position groups.
research_questions.validation_strategy: Nested cross-validation with strict cohort awareness and sensitivity analysis (E-values) for unmeasured draft-capital confounding.

supporting_or_weakening_evidence.supports: Orthogonal sensor components (e.g., braking/fluidity residuals orthogonal to 40-yard dash) showing statistically significant association with `player_career_successes.csv` outcomes.
supporting_or_weakening_evidence.weakens: Small sample size per position group resulting in wide confidence intervals that span zero after multiple-testing correction.

research_questions.known_limitations: Observational associations cannot establish what would have happened had an undrafted prospect been given starter snaps.
research_questions.feasibility_status: Feasible (Tier-1 priority once small CSVs are downloaded)

feature_engineering.name: First-Step Peak Acceleration & Jerk Impulse (0.0s–0.5s Window)
feature_engineering.formula_latex: a_{\text{peak}, 0.5\text{s}} = \max_{t \in [t_0, t_0 + 0.5\text{s}]} a(t), \quad j_{\text{peak}, 0.5\text{s}} = \max_{t \in [t_0, t_0 + 0.5\text{s}]} \frac{a(t + \Delta t) - a(t)}{\Delta t}
feature_engineering.definition: Maximum instantaneous acceleration and finite-difference jerk within the first 5 frames (0.5 seconds at 10 Hz) following movement initiation in a Combine drill or `ball_snap` in regular-season play.
feature_engineering.windowing_and_aggregation: Anchor t_0 at drill start event (or first frame where s > 0.5 yd/s if start event is absent) in Combine tracking, and at `event == 'ball_snap'` in game tracking. Aggregate across frames t_0 to t_0 + 5 per attempt/play, then take 90th percentile across plays per player.
feature_engineering.missing_data_handling: Discard plays/attempts missing the start anchor or containing dropped frame sequences (ΔframeId > 1) inside the 0.5s window.
feature_engineering.leakage_concerns: Low leakage risk when computed strictly within pre-draft `combine_tracking.csv`. When computed on game tracking as a target benchmark, restrict to plays from the specific season being evaluated.
feature_engineering.validation_and_tests: Verify Δt == 0.1s uniformity; assert non-negativity of `a`; verify finite-difference consistency between `s(t+1) - s(t)` and tangential acceleration.

feature_engineering.name: Braking Deceleration Impulse & Entry-to-Exit Speed Ratio
feature_engineering.formula_latex: a_{\text{tangential}}(t) = \frac{s(t) - s(t - \Delta t)}{\Delta t}, \quad I_{\text{brake}} = \sum_{t \in W_{\text{pre-cut}}} \min(0, a_{\text{tangential}}(t)) \cdot \Delta t, \quad R_{\text{speed}} = \frac{s(t_{\text{apex}} + 0.5\text{s})}{s(t_{\text{apex}} - 0.5\text{s})}
feature_engineering.definition: Signed tangential deceleration integrated over the 0.5s braking window prior to a direction-change apex (`t_apex`), paired with the ratio of exit speed (+0.5s post-apex) to entry speed (-0.5s pre-apex).
feature_engineering.units: Tangential Deceleration: yd/s^2; Braking Impulse: yd/s; Speed Ratio: dimensionless [0, 2]
feature_engineering.windowing_and_aggregation: Identify change-of-direction apex `t_apex` as local minimum of speed `s(t)` coinciding with angular path deflection `|Δdir| > 45°`. Window [-5, +5] frames around `t_apex`.
feature_engineering.missing_data_handling: Require at least 5 contiguous frames before and after `t_apex` and entry speed `s(t_apex - 0.5s) >= 3.0 yd/s` to avoid dividing by near-zero stationary speeds.
feature_engineering.leakage_concerns: None when derived from Combine agility drills (3-cone, 20-yard shuttle, positional cuts).
feature_engineering.validation_and_tests: Note that Next Gen Stats column `a` is unsigned magnitude; signed braking MUST be derived via `ds/dt` or projection of acceleration vector onto velocity vector.

feature_engineering.name: Orientation-Direction Divergence (Torso-Path Alignment Angle)
feature_engineering.definition: Smallest circular angle in [0°, 180°] between the direction the player's chest/shoulders are facing (`o`) and the direction their center of mass is moving (`dir`). Quantifies backpedaling (δ ≈ 180°), lateral shuffling/strafe (δ ≈ 90°), and linear forward sprinting (δ ≈ 0°).
feature_engineering.windowing_and_aggregation: Computed frame-by-frame for all frames where `s >= 1.0 yd/s` (since `dir` is undefined/noisy when stationary). Summarized via mean and 90th-percentile speed achieved while in strafe/backpedal posture (`δ_θ > 60°`).
feature_engineering.missing_data_handling: Mask frames where `o` or `dir` is null or `s < 1.0 yd/s`.
feature_engineering.validation_and_tests: Unit test boundary wrapping: e.g., o = 355°, dir = 5° must yield δ_θ = 10°, never 350°.

feature_engineering.name: Peak Angular Hip-Turn Velocity & Transition Speed Retention
feature_engineering.definition: Instantaneous angular velocity of torso orientation (`o`) in degrees per second during transitions (such as a DB opening their hips from backpedal to sprint or a DL spinning/redirecting).
feature_engineering.windowing_and_aggregation: Evaluate joint product `|ω_o(t)| * s(t)` during transition phases where `δ_θ` crosses from >120° (backpedal) to <30° (forward sprint).
feature_engineering.missing_data_handling: Interpolate at most 1 missing frame; exclude sequences with sensor dropouts.
feature_engineering.validation_and_tests: Verify circular difference bounded by [-1800 deg/s, +1800 deg/s] at 10 Hz.

feature_engineering.name: Mass-Adjusted Peak Momentum & Kinetic Power Proxy
feature_engineering.formula_latex: p_{\text{max}} = m_{\text{kg}} \cdot v_{\text{max},\,\text{m/s}}, \quad P_{\text{burst}} = m_{\text{kg}} \cdot a_{\text{m/s}^2}(t) \cdot v_{\text{m/s}}(t)
feature_engineering.definition: Physical linear momentum (kg·m/s) and instantaneous mechanical power proxy (Watts) combining player body mass from `players.csv` / `combine_results.csv` with 10 Hz velocity and acceleration from `combine_tracking.csv`.
feature_engineering.units: Momentum: kg·m/s (using 1 lb = 0.453592 kg, 1 yd = 0.9144 m); Mechanical Power Proxy: Watts (J/s)
feature_engineering.windowing_and_aggregation: Convert `weight` (lbs -> kg) and `s`, `a` (yd -> m) explicitly before multiplication so physical units are SI-consistent.
feature_engineering.missing_data_handling: Fallback to `players.csv` weight if `combine_results.csv` weight is missing.
feature_engineering.leakage_concerns: Use pre-draft Combine weight rather than later veteran roster weight when evaluating pre-draft projection.
feature_engineering.validation_and_tests: Verify dimensional conversion constants (0.45359237 kg/lb and 0.9144 m/yd).

feature_engineering.name: Position-Group Z-Score & Drill Path Tortuosity Index
feature_engineering.definition: Ratio of total curvilinear distance traveled to straight-line Euclidean displacement across a drill segment (tortuosity/curvilinearity), standardized via within-position-group (`g` in {WR, TE, DB, OL, DL}) mean and standard deviation.
feature_engineering.windowing_and_aggregation: Compute per drill segment; fit `μ_g` and `σ_g` strictly on training cohort folds within each position group.
feature_engineering.leakage_concerns: Fit normalization parameters (`μ_g`, `σ_g`) inside cross-validation folds to prevent test-cohort distribution leakage.
feature_engineering.validation_and_tests: Triangle inequality guarantees τ_path >= 1.0 for any valid Euclidean trajectory.

feature_engineering.name: In-Game Route-Break Velocity Retention & Separation Proxy
feature_engineering.definition: On-field regular-season metric measuring a receiver's (WR/TE) speed retention across a route stem break and Euclidean distance to the nearest opposing defender at `pass_arrived` or break apex.
feature_engineering.units: Velocity Retention: dimensionless ratio; Separation: yards (yd)
feature_engineering.windowing_and_aggregation: Filter `player_play.csv` to plays where `routeRan` is a breaking route (e.g., OUT, IN, SLANT, HITCH, COMEBACK, POST, CORNER); aggregate median across a player's season.
feature_engineering.missing_data_handling: Ignore plays aborted by pre-snap penalty or quarterback sack prior to route break.
feature_engineering.leakage_concerns: This is a post-draft regular-season performance measure; use strictly as an analytical outcome/dependent variable, never as a pre-draft predictor.
feature_engineering.validation_and_tests: Verify all players compared on `d_sep(t)` share the exact same `(gameId, playId, frameId)`.

feature_engineering.name: Combine-to-Game Kinematic Transfer Ratio (Functional Play Speed Index)
feature_engineering.definition: Ratio of a player's 99th-percentile on-field regular-season speed to their 99th-percentile Combine drill speed, measuring functional speed translation in pads.
feature_engineering.windowing_and_aggregation: Compute 99th percentile over active play frames (`ball_snap` to `tackle`/`out_of_bounds`) for players with >= 200 tracked play frames.
feature_engineering.missing_data_handling: Require minimum exposure threshold (>= 200 frames) to stabilize the 99th-percentile estimator.
feature_engineering.leakage_concerns: Cross-context research metric bridging Combine and NFL tracking.
feature_engineering.validation_and_tests: Check sensitivity to minimum snap count thresholds.

glossary.definition: Ultra-wideband Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) tags embedded in player shoulder pads that broadcast spatial position and kinematic derivatives 10 times per second (every 100 milliseconds / 0.1s).
glossary.source_label: Officially documented (NFL Football Operations / Next Gen Stats)

glossary.definition: Standardized agility test where a prospect sprints 5 yards to a first cone, returns to the start line, sprints back around the first cone, weaves inside and around a third cone set at a 90-degree angle, and finishes around the second cone. Tests braking, hip sink, and tight-radius bend.

Lateral agility drill in which a prospect starts in a three-point stance, moves 5 yards to one side, touches the line, sprints 10 yards in the opposite direction, touches the line, and sprints 5 yards back through the starting line.
Elapsed time over the first 10 yards of the 40-yard dash. Widely used by scouts to evaluate initial explosive burst off the line of scrimmage, particularly for offensive and defensive linemen.

`o` measures the angle (0°–360°) that a player's chest/shoulder pads are facing, whereas `dir` measures the angle (0°–360°) of the player's instantaneous velocity vector. Their circular difference quantifies backpedaling, strafing, and hip-turn decoupling.
glossary.source_label: Officially documented (NFL Next Gen Stats Schema)

glossary.definition: The rate at which an athlete reduces forward speed (`ds/dt < 0`) over a short time or distance window prior to a cut, while maintaining postural control to transition into re-acceleration.

Coordinate transformation flipping `x -> 120 - x`, `y -> 53.3 - y`, and rotating `o` and `dir` by 180° (modulo 360°) on plays where `playDirection == 'left'`, ensuring all offensive plays move left-to-right.
glossary.source_label: Officially documented (NFL Big Data Bowl Convention)

glossary.definition: Distortion in estimated relationships between Combine traits and NFL outcomes caused by conditioning on players who were drafted and earned regular-season snaps. Because draft selection itself depends on Combine scores, conditioning on roster survival induces collider stratification.
glossary.source_label: Officially documented (Causal Inference & Sports Analytics Methodology)

glossary.definition: Relational error occurring when two tables with multiple rows per entity (such as joining `combine_tracking.csv` directly to `game_tracking_2023.csv` on `nflId` without pre-aggregation, or joining on `playId` without `gameId`) produce a Cartesian product per key.
glossary.source_label: Verified from data (Relational Data Architecture Principle)

glossary.definition: The real-world atomic entity or observation represented by a single row in a table, uniquely identified by its primary or composite key (e.g., one row per player in `players.csv` vs. one row per player-play-frame in `game_tracking_2023.csv`).
